avoid.reason: mongocryptd 16 KiB message limit (CSFLE/QE users only)
avoid.quote: Known Issues: In Version 8.0.18, 8.0.19 SERVER-118428: Changes to mongocryptd limit the maximum size of messages that mongocryptd can receive to 16 KiB. Users may encounter this issue when they send commands larger than 16 KiB through automatic Client-Side Field Level Encryption (CSFLE) or Queryable Encryption. To avoid this bug, skip these versions when you upgrade mongocryptd or use the crypt_shared library.

avoid.reason: Shard can hang during step-up (sharded clusters); fixed in 9.0.4
avoid.quote: 9.0.0, 9.0.1, 9.0.2 SERVER-133518: A shard can hang during step-up when a chunk operation that was interrupted during a prior step-down blocks recovery of a persisted migration recipient. If the hang occurs, the shard cannot become primary, and writes and reads using primary read preference become unavailable on the shard. [...] Fixed in MongoDB 9.0.4.

avoid.reason: Checkpoint data corruption / inconsistency bugs; upgrade to 4.4.9-10+
avoid.quote: This version is not recommended for production use due to the following critical issues: WT-7984 and WT-7995. They are fixed in MongoDB 4.4.9 Community Edition and Percona Server for MongoDB 4.4.9-10. We recommend you to upgrade to Percona Server for MongoDB 4.4.9-10 as soon as possible and run the validate command on every collection on every replica set node.

avoid.reason: 4.4.2-4.4.8 affected by WT-7995; 4.4.3/4.4.4 write bad checkpoint metadata (WT-8395). Go to 4.4.11+ (from 4.4.2-4.4.4 downgrade to 4.4.1 first)
avoid.quote: Note that clusters running versions 4.4.2 - 4.4.8 are affected by the bug WT-7995. See WT-7995 for specific explanation and instructions on running the validate command to check for data inconsistencies. These data inconsistencies can lead to data loss if not identified and repaired at this point between versions 4.4.8 and 4.4.9.

avoid.reason: Data impacting/corrupting bugs introduced in 5.0.1, fixed in 5.0.3
avoid.quote: Beginning with MongoDB 5.0.1, several data impacting or corrupting bugs were introduced. Details are listed below. These bugs are fixed in MongoDB 5.0.3. Percona Server for MongoDB 5.0.3-2 includes the upstream fixes of these bugs.

avoid.reason: Sharding metadata inconsistency with movePrimary at FCV 4.4 or earlier; fixed in 5.0.11
avoid.quote: Another critical issue that affects the production use of this version is SERVER-68511. It causes inconsistency in sharding metadata when running the movePrimary command on the database that has the Feature Compatibility Version (FCV) set to 4.4 or earlier. Affects MongoDB versions 5.0.0 through 5.0.10 and MongoDB 6.0.0. Upgrade to the fixed version of MongoDB 5.0.11 / Percona Server for MongoDB 5.0.11-10 as soon as possible.

avoid.reason: Percona marks these builds as not for production; upgrade to 5.0.11-10+
avoid.quote: We don’t recommend this version for the production use due to the critical issue with sharding metadata inconsistency: SERVER-68511. [...] Upgrade to the fixed version of MongoDB 5.0.11 / Percona Server for MongoDB 5.0.11-10 as soon as possible.

avoid.reason: TTL indexes with expireAfterSeconds NaN expire documents immediately; fixed in 5.0.14 / 6.0.2
avoid.quote: This bug involves TTL indexes with the expireAfterSeconds value of NaN (not-a-number). The TTL indexes are treated as 0 instead of NaN and that resulted in the sudden expiration of TTL-indexed documents in a collection. The bug affects MongoDB 5.0.0 through 5.0.13 and MongoDB 6.0.0 through 6.0.1.

avoid.reason: Sharded time series routing can cause metadata inconsistency; fixed in 5.0.22 / 6.0.12 / 7.0.4
avoid.quote: The issue affects time series sharded collections starting in MongoDB version 5.0.6 through versions 5.0.21, 6.0.11 and 7.0.2. It is fixed upstream in versions 5.0.22, 6.0.12 and 7.0.4 and included in Percona Server for MongoDB 5.0.22-19, 6.0.12-9 and 7.0.4-2.

avoid.reason: Percona marks these builds as not for production (sharded time series routing)
avoid.quote: We don’t recommend this version for production use due to the issue with routing sharding time series collections SERVER-80203 which could result in metadata inconsistency.

avoid.reason: ChunkMap modification during chunk migration could lead to data loss
avoid.quote: SERVER-81966 - Fixed the issue that caused the modification of the original ChunkMap vector during the chunk migration and that could lead to data loss. The issue affects MongoDB versions 4.4.25, 5.0.21, 6.0.10 through 6.0.11 and 7.0.1 through 7.0.2.

upgrade_min_patch.quote: To upgrade a replica set from 7.0-series and earlier, first upgrade all members of the replica set to the latest 8.0-series release, and then follow the procedure to upgrade from MongoDB 8.0 to 9.0.

upgrade_min_patch.condition: only if non-time-series system.buckets collections exist
upgrade_min_patch.quote: MongoDB 8.0.5 and later: You do not need to drop system.buckets collections that aren't time-series collections before you upgrade. However, you must drop or rename them after you complete your upgrade. MongoDB 8.0.4 and earlier: You must drop or rename system.buckets collections that aren't time-series collections before you upgrade.
To upgrade a replica set from 6.0-series and earlier, first upgrade all members of the replica set to the latest 7.0-series release, and then follow the procedure to upgrade from MongoDB 7.0 to 8.0.
To upgrade a replica set from 5.0-series and earlier, first upgrade all members of the replica set to the latest 6.0-series release, and then follow the procedure to upgrade from MongoDB 6.0 to 7.0.

Clusters on versions 4.4.0 and 4.4.1 are safe to upgrade to 4.4.8+ or 5.0.2+ but should upgrade to recommended versions 4.4.11+ or 5.0.5+. Clusters on versions 4.4.2, 4.4.3, or 4.4.4 should downgrade to 4.4.1 and then upgrade to versions 4.4.11+ or 5.0.5+. Clusters running versions 4.4.5 - 4.4.7 can and should upgrade to versions 4.4.11+ or 5.0.5+.

psmdb_tools_unpinned_from._note: From these releases the percona-server-mongodb metapackage depends on percona-server-mongodb-tools without a version (tools use the 100.x numbering). Earlier releases depend on tools of the exact same version, so an apt install of an older release must pin tools too. Source: the Depends field in the Percona apt repositories (repo.percona.com/psmdb-XX/apt), checked 2026-11-03.
